title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'Paradigmes des courbes algébriques' notes, Grothendieck is building a purely combinatorial or group-theoretic model of a surface or curve with boundary or punctures. This model is meant to carry outer actions, so that a group Σ (for example orientations ±1, or a Galois or automorphism group) acting by outer automorphisms on π can be lifted. On the previous page he fixed three things:
- a groupoid Λ whose object set T = Ob Λ plays the role of 'boundary' or tangential base points (the transcription's C);
- an orientation datum for Σ;
- a faithful functor Λ → ⟨π⟩, where ⟨π⟩ is the one-object groupoid with automorphism group π, with π the fundamental group of Π.
Equivalently, this is a family of injections Isom_Λ(t,t') ↪ π, with images π_{t,t'}, compatible with composition.

On this page he imposes the condition that makes the data rigid and compatible with outer operations. For every object t, the subsets π_{t,t'} (t' varying) form a pseudo-partition of π: a partition in which some parts may be empty. In other words, for every λ ∈ π there is exactly one arrow of Λ above λ with source t. In modern terms, Λ → ⟨π⟩ is a covering morphism of groupoids (a discrete fibration, i.e. 'star-bijective').

By the standard equivalence between coverings of ⟨π⟩ and π-sets, this gives:
- an action of π on T;
- an identification Λ ≃ ⟨T, π⟩, the action (translation) groupoid T//π, with the functor to ⟨π⟩ being the canonical projection.
The vertex groups are the stabilizers π_t; geometrically these are the inertia or peripheral subgroups of the boundary components or cusps.

He then adds the hypothesis that the stabilizers π_t are pairwise distinct. Then T can be recovered from subgroups of π, and one gets a family of conjugacy classes or groups indexed by the orbit set J ∈ T/π (one per boundary component or cusp). The Σ-operation on (T, Λ) is to be made compatible with Λ → ⟨π⟩.

He judges this 'pas bien éclairant'. On the next page he switches to an equivalent description via fibre functors Rev(Π) → Ens, i.e. π-sets and contracted products (E ↦ τ° ∧_π E), asking for compatibility isomorphisms F(^γΠ') ≃ F(Π').

The problem served is to encode 'a surface group together with its peripheral system (tangential base points or boundary components)' in a form on which outer actions, such as Galois or mapping-class type actions, are naturally defined. This is the setting of the Esquisse's fundamental groupoids based at tangential points.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. The equivalence between the unique-lifting condition and Λ ≃ action groupoid ⟨T,π⟩ is correct and standard.

Implicit point: requiring the stabilizers π_t to be pairwise distinct within an orbit amounts to π_t being self-normalizing (more precisely, Stab(t) = N_π(π_t) acting freely on the fibre). For surface groups with cyclic peripheral subgroups this holds because peripheral subgroups are malnormal and maximal cyclic. This is not stated on the page.

The margin question (does the ∃! lifting condition reduce to a condition on connected sources, for general groupoid morphisms) is left open. The answer is standard: it is a condition at one object per connected component, by the covering-groupoid theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine (and self-admittedly 'not illuminating') reformulation of standard covering-groupoid theory: unique lifting of arrows ⇒ action groupoid. It is applied to the peripheral structure of a surface group with outer actions. It is a stepping stone, abandoned on the next page in favour of the fibre-functor viewpoint. Nothing here goes beyond what appears in La Longue Marche / Esquisse or the standard literature.
transcription_corrections: 'T_i = ∂Λ' should read 'T = Ob Λ' (the image shows '∀t ∈ T = Ob Λ'; the previous page defines the object set as Ob Λ). The same applies to 'opération de π sur T = Ob Λ'.
'on a exigé[?]' is more likely 'on va exiger'.
'(t' ∈ T variable)' — fine. 'pseudo-partition de π' confirmed.
Margin is approximately: 'examiner si bien la condition ∃! de remontages de flèches : origines connexes, pour morphismes de groupoïdes ...'.
'et la façon de réinterpréter' — plausible. 'Dans [-...-] l'hypothèse de plus que les stabilisateurs π_t sont distincts' confirmed.
'une famille de groupes T_J / J ∈ T̄ = T/π' — the symbol before /J is uncertain; it likely denotes groups or conjugacy classes indexed by orbits J ∈ T/π.
'opération de Σ sur (T, Λ)' and 'compatible avec op. de Σ' confirmed.
